doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: The 1960s Basie band versus the 1938 band
summary: Ross and Zoot Sims argued over the two Basie bands; the early band used head arrangements.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: I knew a lot of guys in Basie’s band. I knew Snooky and Frank Foster and Frank Wess and Charlie Fowlkes and Joe Newman and Freddie Green and Eddie Jones. Like the 60s.
Yeah. It was that nice thing.

Because Zoot and I used to argue. I was very fond of that band, of that period when Snooky was playing lead, you know, Sonny Payne, Eddie Jones. And Zoot and I used to argue whether the ‘38 band with Sweets and Buck and all those guys, which one was better. And they were both great. I think probably the one from the 60s might be a little rehearsed a little more or something.
Yeah, but the earlier band was like an original.
They both — you could make a case for either one of them certainly.
Wasn’t the earlier band playing more head arrangements?
They had a lot of head arrangements, yeah. “Jumpin’ at the Woodside” at first it wasn’t even written out I heard.
